summary_ja: 金融庁長官の承認を受けた期待エクスポージャー方式（与信相当額＝α×実効EPE、α＝1.4）の算出方法、ストレス期間を含む実効EPE、αの独自推計（下限一・二）と長官指定、担保の勘案、リスクのマージン期間、個別誤方向リスク、相対ネッティングの要件等を定める。
summary_en: The internal model method (expected exposure method), with FSA approval: exposure = α × effective EPE (α = 1.4), using the higher of current and stressed EPE; own estimates of α (floor 1.2) or an FSA-set α; collateral, margin period of risk, specific wrong-way risk and netting requirements.

terms.ja: 期待エクスポージャー
期待エクスポージャー計測モデル

paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach may, where it has received the approval of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency, calculate credit equivalent amounts using the expected exposure method.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach uses the expected exposure method, for each netting set (collateral included in the netting set being limited to eligible financial collateral; the same applies hereinafter), the credit equivalent amount shall be the amount calculated by the formula listed in item (i), the effective EPE required for calculating the formula listed in that item shall be the amount calculated by the formula listed in item (ii), and the effective EE_{tk} listed in that item shall be the amount calculated by the formula listed in item (iii); provided, however, that where the longest maturity of all transactions making up the netting set is less than one year, in calculating the effective EPE specified in item (ii), the effective EPE weighted-averaged by Δt_{k} of that item up to that maturity shall be used. (i) Credit equivalent amount = α × effective EPE α is 1.4 (where there are specific characteristics relating to the counterparty's credit risk, a more conservative α according to those characteristics shall be used). (ii) {{F:p111i2}} n is such that t_{n} is one year. Δt_{k} is t_{k} − t_{k−1}. (iii) Effective EE_{tk} = max(effective EE_{tk−1}, EE_{tk}) EE_{tk} is the average of all positive exposure amounts at future time t_{k} (hereinafter referred to as "expected exposure"); provided, however, that effective EE_{t0} shall be the current exposure (meaning the greater of zero and the amount of loss that would arise from the default of the counterparty relating to the netting set subject to the calculation of expected exposure, calculated based on the market values of the transactions included in that netting set; the same applies in item (v) of the following paragraph, in paragraph (8) and in Article 135, paragraph (7)).

In calculating the credit equivalent amount listed in item (i) of the preceding paragraph, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall satisfy all of the following requirements. (i) That it uses, of the effective EPE of the whole portfolio calculated using current market data and the effective EPE of the whole portfolio calculated using data that includes an appropriate stress period, the effective EPE that results in the larger credit risk-weighted assets (excluding the CVA risk equivalent amount). (ii) That the terms of transactions (including the notional amount, maturity, reference assets, collateral thresholds and the contents of legally effective bilateral netting contracts) are properly stored in a database (meaning a collection of information for calculating credit equivalent amounts under the expected exposure method, systematically structured so that information on a specific counterparty can be retrieved; the same applies in the following item) and are reflected in a timely, comprehensive and conservative manner in the system built to measure expected exposure (hereinafter referred to as the "expected exposure model"). (iii) That a reconciliation process between the expected exposure model and the database has been established in order to confirm on an ongoing basis that the terms of transactions are properly reflected in the expected exposure model. (iv) That a process for properly confirming the legal effectiveness of netting contracts has been established. (v) That, in calculating the effective EPE of the whole portfolio using current market data in item (i), current exposure is measured using current market data at least once every three months, and the parameters of the expected exposure model are estimated using market data for at least the most recent three years; provided, however, that market-implied data (meaning market data derived by working back from actual transaction prices, etc. observed in the market; the same applies in the following item) may be used in estimating the parameters of the expected exposure model. (vi) That, in calculating the effective EPE of the whole portfolio using data that includes an appropriate stress period in item (i), it uses three years of market data (including the stress period) satisfying all of the following requirements, or market-implied data drawn from an appropriate stress period: (a) The stress period is consistent with a period of widening credit spreads observed in the market for a representative portfolio (meaning a set of transactions with a sufficient number of counterparties, constructed to represent its own portfolio based on the main risk factors and the effect of correlations; the same applies in Article 51, item (v)); provided, however, that where credit spreads are not observed in the market, credit spreads estimated for each counterparty based on region, rating and industry may be used. (b) It is consistent with the calibration method of the expected exposure model used in calculating the effective EPE in the preceding item. (c) The adequacy of the effective EPE is assessed by constructing benchmark portfolios that are vulnerable to the main risk factors and measuring the exposure amounts of those benchmark portfolios.

Where all of the following requirements are satisfied, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach may, notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (2), item (i), estimate α in the formula listed in that item (referred to simply as "α" in this paragraph and the following paragraph); provided, however, that where the estimated α is less than 1.2, α shall be 1.2. (i) That α is estimated as the value obtained by dividing the amount of economic capital (meaning capital used in risk management, capital allocation, performance evaluation and other internal management; the same applies hereinafter in this paragraph) relating to exposures to all counterparties by the amount of economic capital where EPE is regarded as an outstanding loan balance. In this case, EPE shall be the value calculated by the following formula; provided, however, that where the longest maturity of all transactions making up the netting set is less than one year, in calculating EPE, the EPE weighted-averaged by Δt_{k} of this item up to that maturity shall be used. {{F:p113i0}} n is such that t_{n} is one year. Δt_{k} is t_{k} − t_{k−1}. (ii) That, in calculating the amount of economic capital, the main sources of stochastic dependency in the distribution of market values of transactions or portfolios of transactions across all counterparties are captured. (iii) That the method of using the model for calculating the amount of economic capital, the specification of parameters and the composition of the portfolio are reasonable and consistent. (iv) That α is updated at least once every three months, and that, whenever there is a significant change in the composition of the portfolio, an update reflecting that change is made. (v) That α takes into account the granularity of exposures (meaning the distribution of the individual netting sets included in the exposures). (vi) That the model for calculating the amount of economic capital is validated by persons with sufficient competence who are independent of its development. (vii) That the model risk of the model for calculating the amount of economic capital is assessed and changes in α are evaluated. (viii) That, where the model for calculating the amount of economic capital simulates market risk and credit risk together, the increase in volatility or correlation in a downturn is taken into account by including the volatilities and correlation coefficients of market risk factors in the credit risk factors. (ix) That the method of calculating the amount of economic capital is documented.

Where any of the following applies and the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency has designated a value of α, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall calculate credit equivalent amounts using that value of α. (i) Where the counterparty credit risk is excessively concentrated. (ii) Where there are excessive exposures with general wrong-way risk (meaning the risk that the exposure amount increases because the counterparty's PD is positively correlated with general market risk factors; the same applies in Article 51, items (iii)(g) and (xiii)). (iii) Where the exposures to multiple counterparties are highly correlated. (iv) Where there are specific characteristics relating to the counterparty's credit risk, or where there are significant problems in the model validation provided in Article 51, item (iv).

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach reflects in the expected exposure model the effect of collateral under a margin agreement with the counterparty relating to a netting set, it may measure the effective EPE provided in paragraph (2), item (ii) by using, in calculating the effective EE_{tk} provided in item (iii) of that paragraph, EE_{tk} that takes into account the effect of that collateral; provided, however, that the effect of collateral under a margin agreement providing that collateral may be requested from the counterparty when its credit standing deteriorates shall not be reflected.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach reflects in the expected exposure model the effect of collateral under a margin agreement, it shall, in calculating the credit equivalent amount provided in paragraph (2), item (i), take into account the following elements of the transactions. (i) The contractual form of the margin agreement. (ii) The margin period of risk provided in paragraph (11). (iii) The frequency with which collateral is requested from the counterparty. (iv) The threshold. (v) The minimum transfer amount.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach uses eligible financial collateral as a credit risk mitigation technique in calculating the credit equivalent amount provided in paragraph (2), item (i), it shall reflect the credit risk mitigation effect in the process of calculating current exposure.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall measure effective EPE in the expected exposure model taking into account the possibility that the distribution of exposures is not normal.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach measures effective EPE using the method provided in paragraph (6), it shall take into account the change in the market value of transactions with the counterparty within the margin period of risk.

The margin period of risk in the preceding paragraph shall be as specified in each of the following items according to the category of netting set listed in that item. (i) Netting sets for which the amount of collateral is adjusted by daily mark-to-market: the period specified in (a) through (d) below according to the category of netting set listed in (a) through (d). (a) Netting sets consisting only of repo-style transactions (excluding those falling under (b) or (c)): 5 business days. (b) Netting sets containing illiquid collateral or derivative transactions that are difficult to replace: 20 business days. (c) Netting sets in which the number of transactions exceeded 5,000 at any point during the Ultimate Designated Parent Company quarter immediately preceding the Ultimate Designated Parent Company quarter that includes the calculation reference date: 20 business days. (d) Netting sets other than those listed in (a) through (c): 10 business days. (ii) Netting sets for which the amount of collateral is adjusted by mark-to-market every N days (N being an integer of two or more): F + N − 1 F is the margin period of risk calculated under the provisions of the preceding item.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding paragraph, where, during the two most recent consecutive Ultimate Designated Parent Company quarters before the Ultimate Designated Parent Company quarter that includes the calculation reference date, there have been three or more instances in which, for any netting set listed in item (i)(a) through (d) or item (ii) of that paragraph, a close-out period exceeding the margin period of risk in that paragraph was required because of disputes over margin calls, the margin period of risk for that netting set during the next two consecutive Ultimate Designated Parent Company quarters shall be a period at least twice the margin period of risk in that paragraph.

Where, in the transactions making up a netting set, a legal relationship exists between the counterparty and the reference entity and specific wrong-way risk (meaning the risk that the future exposure amount to a specific counterparty increases or decreases in high correlation with that counterparty's PD; the same applies hereinafter) has been identified, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall exclude that transaction from that netting set.

In calculating the credit risk-weighted assets relating to transactions for which a legal relationship exists between the counterparty and the reference entity and specific wrong-way risk has been identified, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall take into account the characteristics of that specific wrong-way risk.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach reflects the effect of collateral in assets other than cash under a margin agreement, it shall satisfy the condition specified in each of the following items according to the case listed in that item. (i) Where the effect of the collateral is modelled (meaning building and calibrating the expected exposure model so that it quantitatively reflects the effects of specific contractual terms, market developments, etc.; the same applies in the following item): the effect of the collateral and the exposures of repo-style transactions and margin lending and similar overseas transactions are modelled simultaneously. (ii) Where the effect of the collateral is not modelled: the comprehensive approach using the standard supervisory haircuts provided in Section 6, Subsection 3, Division 2 is used.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach may take into account the effect of a legally effective bilateral netting contract covering derivative transactions and repo-style transactions and margin lending and similar overseas transactions only where all of the following conditions are satisfied. (i) That, where an event occurs that allows one party to terminate the transactions (including the counterparty's failure to perform an obligation to deliver cash or securities, to provide additional collateral or another obligation, and the occurrence of insolvency, a decision to commence bankruptcy proceedings, a decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings, a decision to commence reorganization proceedings, an order to commence special liquidation or similar events; the same applies in Article 51, item (xiv) and Article 79, paragraph (1), item (i)), the other party can promptly terminate all transactions under that bilateral netting contract and turn them into a single claim or obligation. (ii) That it has been properly confirmed that the bilateral netting contract is effective in light of all laws and regulations (including foreign laws and regulations) relevant to it. (iii) That the credit equivalent amount taking into account the effect of the bilateral netting contract is closely integrated into the normal risk management procedures. (iv) That all documents relating to the bilateral netting contract are properly retained.

For trade exposures to indirect clearing participants arising from carrying out, as a direct clearing participant, securities clearing brokerage provided in Article 2, paragraph (27) of the Act relating to indirect clearing participants' trade exposures to qualifying central counterparties, commodity clearing transactions provided in Article 2, paragraph (20) of the Commodity Derivatives Act relating to indirect clearing participants' trade exposures to qualifying central counterparties, or other brokerage relating to indirect clearing participants' trade exposures to qualifying central counterparties or similar overseas transactions, the margin period of risk of the netting sets listed in paragraph (11), item (i) may, notwithstanding that item, be 5 business days.
